newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil -Eases as poor demand takes its toll.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil -Eases as poor demand takes its toll.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market dipped as Chinese importers took a breather amid persistent talks of unsold cargoes in March, traders said on Monday.
"The Chinese have absorbed most of the April cargoes from South Korea, they are looking at May but would like to test the waters first before taking the plunge," one South Korean trader said.
The trader said in April, a major shipped about two to three cargoes to Hong Kong and another local trader also moved about the same volumes into southern China.
Bids for South Korean supplies in May were heard at $1.00 per tonne above Singapore spot quotes with sellers at close to $2.00-premiums, said traders.

A few majors attributed the dip to a surplus of imports in March. "The increase in March imports at about two million tonnes compared to January's 1.2 million tonnes were also putting pressure on prices," one major said.
"The weak bunker demand with shipowners buying only top-up cargoes and the lack of demand here is not making things any better," another major said.
Traders said prices in Singapore are overpriced, with Rotterdam offering more competitive levels.
They said South Korean supplies would be cut as refiners begin their shutdown season in May.
"This would help move the market up as China will have to look towards South Asia for supplies," said one trader.
In the swaps market, paper dipped by around $2 per tonne from Friday's quotes to be quoted at $95.50/$96.50 for May and June at $94.50/$95.60 per tonne.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
